The Chirps and the Welcome Tree

A Roof That Sang in the Rain

When rain came to the garden, Daisy knew exactly what to do. She spread a broad leaf over the Everybody Day bench. Three fat drops ran off its tip. She sat down underneath, perfectly dry.

She invited Frog to try it. He settled in. Pat. Pat. Pat. His toes stayed dry. His nose stayed dry. His great wide smile grew smaller and smaller.

“Is the roof too low?” Daisy asked. She lifted it. “Is the seat too hard?” She added moss. Frog sank so far into the moss that only his eyes showed.

“I came to hear the rain,” said the moss. “At home it drums on the reeds. In here it sounds like someone counting potatoes.” Pat. Pat. Pat. Daisy listened. It did.

“Show me your favorite sound,” she said. Frog led her to a curled leaf. Rain rolled down its spine and struck a flat stone. Plinka-ponk! Another stone answered plink.

Daisy angled a second leaf over the far end of the bench. Its tip sent drops onto two stones. At one end you could listen to plinka-ponk. At the other you could still count potatoes.

Moth folded her wings at the quiet end. Frog tapped his toes at the noisy end. Daisy tried the place between them. “Oh,” she said, as a stray drop landed on her bill. “Mine has a surprise.”

On her leaf for the Welcome Tree Daisy drew two roofs and a raindrop. She listened to the rain all the way home. It had quite a lot to say about potatoes.

Read together

Which part of the rain would you want to sit beside?
